objects.original: One smooth positive g approximates f and the noise amplitude sqrt(2f).
objects.reconstructed: One existential g, with coefficient error and squared noise error in the same conjunction.
objects.evidence: The proof obtains g once from the preceding theorem at epsilon/2 and returns that same g.

domains.original: Real functions on R; Lebesgue set integrals on [a,b]; clarified measurable representative for the noise integral.
domains.reconstructed: Total Real.sqrt, zero at negative inputs, under volume.restrict (Icc a b).
domains.evidence: The revised source and lesson explicitly state the total-root convention or any measurable nonnegative a.e. representative. Arbitrary negative null values of f do not alter the integral.

quantifiers.original: For every admissible data set there is one g meeting both strict error tolerances.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universal data binders then one existential g with both inequalities.
quantifiers.evidence: No separate choice for the noise amplitude and no uniform g across tolerances are asserted.

assumptions.original: a<=b, C>=0, epsilon>0, f Borel measurable and in [0,C] a.e. on the interval.
assumptions.reconstructed: hab,hC,hε,hf,hRange, identical to the coefficient theorem.
assumptions.evidence: The private helper needs nonnegative inputs only at good points, supplied a.e. by hgRange and hRange. It adds no hypothesis to the public theorem.

conclusion.original: g smooth, 0<g<=C+epsilon on [a,b], both integrals strictly <epsilon.
conclusion.reconstructed: ContDiff, interval bounds, L1 norm error <epsilon and squared Real.sqrt norm error <epsilon.
conclusion.evidence: sq_abs identifies squared norm with the square of the difference; hAInt and hgL1 give the strict factor-two estimate.

scopes.original: Includes zero coefficient, zero-length interval and negative values on exceptional null sets; no positive lower bound on f.
scopes.reconstructed: Zero inputs allowed by the helper, a.e. comparison, integrability from domination, total root at exceptional points.
scopes.evidence: No division by sqrt(f) or a positive coefficient lower bound occurs. Positivity of g is asserted on the interval only.

constant_dependencies.original: Use T1 at epsilon/2 and dominate squared noise error by 2|g-f|.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: half_pos hε selects the witness; hABound and integral_const_mul yield integral A<=2*integral|g-f|<epsilon.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The upper bound C+epsilon/2 is relaxed to C+epsilon; the strict coefficient error is also relaxed to epsilon.

proof_review: Read the entire smoothing module. Independently checked the private sq_sqrt_sub_sqrt_le_abs_sub: in x<=y, the desired gap is 2*sqrt(x)*(sqrt(y)-sqrt(x))>=0; the other order is symmetric. Real.sq_sqrt uses precisely hx,hy and monotonicity includes zero. The public proof applies it a.e. to 2g,2f, rewrites squared absolute value and the factor two, proves A measurable and integrable by domination, then integrates and uses the same half-tolerance witness.

boundaries: Both helper inputs may be zero.
The output g is strictly positive only where stated; f can be negative on a null set.
Noise error is squared amplitude error, not an unsquared L1 amplitude estimate.
